correctness.rationale: Gaussian integration gives the exact normalized identity with a positive cross-envelope; signs of two quadratic exponents give sharp outer conical exclusion and decay on every interior ray. Each sufficiently large cosine node has a single transverse perturbative zero, yielding the explicit exponential phase error and quadratic count. Boundary-ray conditions are exactly the inequalities u<1 or v<1. The balanced-ray positivity threshold gives an exact first-zero bracket; separate expansions at fixed amplitude c=1 and c!=1 prove epsilon*T_first^2 -> 4pi and epsilon^2*T_first^2 -> 8p log((c+1/c)/2). Direct numerical integrals and roots were reproduced by CHECKER.py, but the proofs do not depend on finite tests.

value.rationale: For all strictly positive Schwartz two-scale Gaussian windows with strictly positive Fourier transforms, a formerly hidden infinite family of exact ambiguity zeros is confined to a sharp cone determined only by Gaussian widths. Quantitative zero density, amplitude-dependent boundary-ray admission, and the two distinct rates at which zeros escape when widths coalesce supply structural information relevant to stable time-frequency window selection, beyond algebraic evaluation of a single cross-Gaussian transform.
